hook.line: Sooner or later, in every argument, someone is right. Tomás needs to be able to say so warmly, and to say *no* just as clearly when someone else is wrong.
hook.es: Tienes toda la razón, debí avisarte antes.
hook.en: You're absolutely right, I should have told you sooner.

examples.es: Tienes toda la razón, debí avisarte antes.
examples.en: You're absolutely right, I should have told you sooner. (to a friend)

examples.es: Usted tiene toda la razón, don Hernando.
Estás muy equivocado si piensas que voy a ceder.
examples.en: You're very wrong if you think I'm going to give in. (to a man, friend)

examples.es: No estoy en absoluto de acuerdo con ese análisis.
examples.en: I don't agree with that analysis at all.

examples.es: No, no, eso no es cierto.

rule:
To say someone is right, Spanish has *razón*, and you *have* it, as you have hunger: *Tienes razón*. Add *toda* for *completely*: *Tienes toda la razón.* To say they are wrong: *No tienes razón*, or *Estás equivocado* (*equivocada* for a woman).

These aim at the person, so agreeing is warm and disagreeing is sharp.

For disagreeing with an idea, aim at the claim: *No estoy en absoluto de acuerdo*, or the short *¡En absoluto!* or *Eso no es cierto*.

*En absoluto* always means *not at all*, never *absolutely yes*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these expressions of strong agreement and disagreement.

readAndPick.es: No estoy en absoluto de acuerdo.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tienes* or *tiene*, then type the whole sentence: ___ toda la razón. (You're completely right, to a friend.)
yourTurn.why: A friend is *tú*, and *tú* ends in *-s*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tiene* or *tienes*, then type the whole sentence: Usted ___ toda la razón. (You're completely right, formal.)
yourTurn.why: *Usted* takes the same verb form as *he* or *she*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: You're wrong. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: You *have* reason in Spanish, so being wrong is *not having* it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I don't agree at all.
yourTurn.answer: No estoy en absoluto de acuerdo.
yourTurn.why: *En absoluto* goes before *de acuerdo* to strengthen the *no*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: You're very wrong. (to a woman)
yourTurn.why: A woman gets the *-a* ending on *equivocada*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Tienes razón. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it more complete: Tienes razón. (You're absolutely right, to a friend.)

pitfalls.why: Almost. In Spanish you *have* reason, so the verb is *tener*.
Almost. *En absoluto* on its own always means *not at all*.

personal: Think of someone who was right last week. Tell them so, starting with *Tienes toda la razón*.
